pages.text: "The water's steaming! I don't like hot things!" Steam rose from a big yard pot. Grandma had finished heating it and stirred with a dipper. Holding the scarf, Yuki backed away.
"I'll go to bed without washing!" Yuki hid behind the shed. Brown dog Momo followed, tail wagging, and lay beside them. Grandma pretended not to see and folded a towel by the pot.
Sitting behind the shed, Yuki's back felt sticky. Grass bits clung to their neck. "Why am I so itchy?" Yuki scratched hard.
Grandma floated a plank on the water. "Look!" The wide board bobbed on top. Yuki peeked from behind the shed.
"The pot's bottom is hot, so step on this plank to get in." Grandma tested the water with fingertips; Yuki with toes. "Oh, it's just right!" Yuki's eyes widened.
Yuki stepped on the plank and slid into the water. Splash! Warm water rose to their shoulders. "Rising Steam, Splash!" Yuki patted the water.
Grandma poured with the dipper and rubbed Yuki's back. Grass bits washed from their neck. Splashed beside the pot, Momo shook all over.
Out of the pot, the evening breeze felt cool on Yuki's body. Their neck no longer itched. "Baths can feel this refreshing?" Yuki stretched their shoulders.
The next evening, Yuki untied the scarf alone and ran to the pot. Counting on fingers, Yuki said, "One, test the water! Two, step on the plank! Three, sink in to my neck! Grandma, float the plank!"
Grandma wrapped clean, dry Yuki in a towel and hugged them. Water that looked hot had become the most refreshing water play. "Grandma, tomorrow again—Rising Steam, Splash!"
